hero.title: PPE detection for construction site safety
hero.description: PPE detection adds construction safety monitoring to your existing CCTV. Spot missing hard hats, vests, and gloves and alert supervisors with evidence.

problems.title: Where do manual PPE checks fall short?
problems.description: Crews move between work areas throughout the shift. Supervisors cannot check every worker on every camera continuously.

items.title: Workers enter without protection
items.description: Missing hard hats, vests, or gloves can go unnoticed as crews enter monitored work areas.

items.title: Supervisors find violations too late
items.description: Footage reviewed after a shift cannot help supervisors address missing PPE while workers are exposed.

items.title: Compliance records have gaps
items.description: Scattered notes and manual checks leave safety teams without consistent evidence of when and where PPE violations occurred.

solution.title: Detect missing PPE across existing cameras
solution.description: Ailytics adds PPE detection to existing CCTV, with models built for rain, dust, and low light. Supervisors receive event evidence to review missing protection and respond during the shift.

features.title: PPE checks your team can act on

faq.question: What is PPE detection for construction sites?
faq.answer: PPE stands for personal protective equipment. Ailytics uses computer vision to detect missing hard hats, vests, and gloves in existing CCTV views. When it detects an event, it can notify supervisors with the frame, time, and location. This adds ongoing camera monitoring to the inspections and safety procedures your construction team already uses.

faq.question: Can PPE detection use our existing construction CCTV cameras?
faq.answer: Yes. Ailytics connects to existing IP cameras and compatible recording systems through RTSP or ONVIF, which are methods for accessing video feeds. You do not need to replace your cameras. Camera position, visibility, and the size of PPE items in the image affect coverage, so bring representative site footage to the demo for assessment.

faq.question: Can Ailytics detect missing hard hats, safety vests, and gloves?
faq.answer: These are the PPE items covered by Ailytics' detection capabilities. Your team can configure checks to match site requirements. Each camera must show enough detail to assess the selected item, especially smaller items such as gloves. During the demo, review representative camera views and the PPE requirements for the work areas you want to monitor.

faq.question: Does PPE detection work in rain, dust, and low light?
faq.answer: Ailytics' models are built for harsh construction conditions, including rain, dust, and low light. Detection still depends on usable footage and a clear enough view of the worker and equipment being checked. Share examples from different shifts and weather conditions so the team can assess where your current cameras provide suitable PPE coverage.

faq.question: Can we reduce repeated PPE alerts?
faq.answer: Set grace periods and cooldowns per camera and person to reduce repeat notifications from the same violation. Match these settings to your work areas and the way supervisors respond during a shift.

faq.question: Can PPE footage stay on our construction site's network?
faq.answer: Yes. The Ailyssa detection engine can run on edge, on-premise, or cloud infrastructure. On-premise deployment allows data to stay on-site. Your IT and safety teams can review the deployment approach together, including video access, storage, network requirements, and how supervisors receive alerts. Ailytics is ISO/IEC 27001 certified. Discuss your project's requirements during the demo.

faq.question: Can we combine PPE detection with other construction safety checks?
faq.answer: Yes. PPE detection can sit alongside [open edge detection](/use-cases/open-edge-detection), [suspended load detection](/use-cases/suspended-load-safety), [pedestrian detection](/use-cases/pedestrian-detection-system) near machinery, and restricted-area alerts in the same platform. Select the checks that fit each work area and its camera coverage. See the [construction industry page](/industries/construction) for how Ailytics combines safety monitoring with workforce tracking and visual progress records across a construction site.
